This paper examines the impact of opportunity inequity on the distribution of income across an economy. It is defined when individuals receiving identical income offers demonstrate differing probabilities of securing the corresponding jobs. The study analyzes how such inequity influences both actual income distributions and perceived equity, noting specifically that its adverse effects intensify as the GolD index of the underlying labor market rises.

We extend the definition of quantum $K$ theory for projective varieties, generalizing work previously done in homology by Fock and Goncharov. Our framework utilizes an affine variety known as $Y_X$, defined through the representation theory of the linear space associated with the variety $X$. For projective varieties $X$, we establish a correspondence between effective stable morphisms and the integral points on ${}^{cl}$ ${Y_X}$, analogous to the Fock-Goncharov pairing for hyperbolic geometry. Furthermore, we define quantum $K$ homology and demonstrate an equivalence between quantum $K$ cohomology and quantum ${Y_X}$, mirroring the isotropic relations found in hyperbolic geometry. It remains an open challenge to develop a version of mirror symmetple in the quantum ${Y_X}$ context.

We introduce a novel local attribution approach designed to diagnose data quality issues within machine learning pipelines. In an increasingly automated environment where machine learning (ML) is integral to business strategy, the efficacy of business objectives closely depends on the quality of input data. Although businesses invest heavily in enhancing data and model performance, existing methods for identifying data flaws often rely on isolated statistical tests that neglect the feedback loops created by downstream machine learning models. We address this gap by incorporating the model's influence into our diagnostic framework, specifically through an innovative adaptation of Shapley value attribution to examine the connection between input stimuli and output predictions. By analyzing how variations in input data traverse the learning pipeline, we can pinpoint specific data anomalies. While not the first method to explore end-to-end pipeline diagnostics, our approach offers a distinct advantage: it requires no additional hyperparameters, remains easy to implement, and is highly efficient to compute. We validate the utility of our technique using a real-world case study involving credit card default detection, demonstrating how our method successfully identifies subtle, intricate data defects that elude conventional approaches.

The primary radio emission mechanism in globular clusters (GCs) is widely understood to be magnetic radio recombination lines resulting from massive stars, specifically from the ionization of their hydrogen-helium stellar winds. Although small in number, these stars are so luminous that they can dominate a GC's total radio output; consequently, the rate of stellar mass shedding and the density of ions near the stellar plasma zone are the primary determinants of a cluster's radio brightness. This research utilizes data from the MAVERIC project (Massive X-ray and Radio Emission in Clusters) to examine how radio properties scale with dynamical state. We utilized a sample of 14 radio-emitting GCs, categorized into four groups based on their dynamical status: coresolved, core-collapsed, unrelaxed, and core-collapsed. This study highlights that both core-collapsed and core-supported GCs exhibit a distinct dependence of their radio characteristics on dynamical evolution, suggesting that stellar density plays a pivotal role in determining a cluster's radio luminosity.

Two-dimensional megavoltage (2D MV) imaging captures snapshots of a patient's anatomy during the delivery of a therapy beam, offering a method to verify patient alignment. Due to the inherent limitations of these scans in terms of resolution and tissue context, accurately aligning these images with a full-body three-dimensional tomographic map (typically a computed tomography or kV image) remains a significant challenge. This study introduces a deep learning framework utilizing a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed to automatically register 2D MV images to kilovoltage (kV) anatomy. Tumor structures were extracted via an active contour model guided by deep segmentation networks. The proposed algorithm was trained on a dataset comprising 1,024 pairs of synchronized MV and CT images, with performance subsequently evaluated on an independent test set. The evaluation involved assessing both the speed of the network's inference and the geometric accuracy of the derived transformations using a statistical evaluation of translation and rotation errors. The results demonstrated an extremely rapid inference rate, processing a pair of images every 0.1 seconds on a single GPU. Furthermore, the extracted pose parameters exhibited a mean translation estimation error below 1.6 mm and a mean rotation error under 0.7 degrees. These metrics suggest the proposed active contour-driven, CNN-based registration method is highly effective for the fast, automatic alignment of MV imaging and kV tomography.

Does the distribution of independent particles exhibiting only nonclassical individual properties generate nonlocal correlations that surpass classical limits? We address this inquiry within the single-mode Fock space framework, where quantum states represent single-particle states and multi-party states arise from their tensor product distributions across multiple modes. We introduce a model of single-particle entanglement to characterize single-state purity; notably, all multi-particle states constructed from single-mode pure states (that are not themselves single-particle entangled) produce only local correlations. We demonstrate that states formed from single-particle entangled single modes generate nonlocal correlations satisfying the Pusey-Fermer-Thouless (PFT) inequality, a threshold beyond which local hidden variable models fail. Furthermore, we show that single-particle entanglement enables single-particle steering between distant single modes, implying that the classical intuition requiring strictly classical multi-particle states for nonlocal or steerable behavior is fundamentally flawed.

This study examines the latest literature on Blockchain-supported Federated Learning (FL) within Internet of Vehicles (IoVs). As IoVs face escalating security and privacy challenges, traditional learning models are no longer adequate, necessitating the adoption of FL to train machine learning models on data kept locally on devices. Nevertheless, direct FL implementations in IoVs encounter obstacles, prompting researchers to integrate blockchain solutions to enhance privacy, security, and trust. A detailed analysis compares the strengths and limitations of these approaches, outlining a taxonomy of current methods and proposing seven key requirements for future blockchain-enabled FL frameworks for IoVs. Finally, this research offers cutting-edge insights and anticipates potential advancements in this evolving field.

Building upon prior work that contrasts toric code architectures with fully connected quantum circuits, this study continues the comparison by analyzing systems where only local three-qubit operations are permitted. Our analysis indicates that both architectures exhibit nearly identical performance when applying two-qubit operations locally around each code word. Furthermore, applying the Steane cross-check operator to the data within the toric code yields marginal improvements in application fidelity relative to implementing the operator directly in the circuit without verification. Additionally, both approaches maintain comparable resilience against drift-induced phase shifts; however, we observe a significant enhancement in both peak fidelity and lifetime when employing operator application within a toric code environment that incorporates a verification step capable of correcting such drifts.

While Channel State Information (CSI) feedback remains a primary bottleneck in future cellular architectures (both TDD and FDD), the uplink reference signal overhead for FDD channels has further intensified due to the necessity of estimating downlink and uplink channel conditions separately. Leveraging FDD channel reciprocity estimation, this study explores FDD-unique joint channel and codebook optimization strategies, specifically focusing on enhancing the generation of channel samples for MMSE-based estimation. Regarding the codebook aspect, we introduce a novel, high-performance graph-based driver for codebook matrix generation that surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques. In terms of channel processing, we propose a refined codebook-dependent derivation method for the matrix used in sample generation, improving upon traditional MMSE MM matrices to better align with actual feedback conditions. These suggested innovations are validated through comprehensive simulations covering various channel environments, user densities, and operational parameters. Validation results confirm that when applied to FDD channels, the proposed methodology outperforms existing codebooks by improving achievable spectral efficiency by up to 10.66% and reducing the bit overhead required for feedback by up to 18.38%.

We investigate whether Population III remnants in Nuclear Star Clusters (NSCs) constitute a detectable source of gravitational waves for LISA. Using a recent framework for simulating Pop III remnant dynamics, we conducted extensive population synthesis simulations of massive stars in low-mass galaxies ($10^8 \le M_{\text{gal}} < 10^9 \,M_\odot$). Our results indicate that in approximately 10–20\% of such galaxies, a supermassive black hole (SMBH) forms not from direct collapse, but through the merger of multiple Pop III black holes. Consequently, about 50\% of all galaxies hosting BH-BH systems formed from first-generation stars. In these cases, mergers occur rapidly, with a median timescale of 1.5 Gyr, and are frequently facilitated by interactions with the surrounding stellar environment. We find that BH-BH systems formed via mergers between two individual Pop III black holes yield the most favorable detection rates for LISA, occurring within its frequency band 30\% of the time, with median frequency-$1/3$ amplitude values of $f^{1/3} = 2.8 \times 10^{-21}\,\text{Hz}^{1/3}$. In our expanding society, higher education serves as a primary pathway, fostering an environment where research and development flourish. Within this ecosystem, publishing in top-tier international conferences and journals stands as a pivotal indicator of institutional efficacy. Nevertheless, an unexamined assumption persists among educational administrators that a high volume of publications automatically signifies the generation of valuable knowledge. This study critically examines the correlation between knowledge acquisition, knowledge generation, and scientific production to address these concerns. It further explores whether the quantity of publications genuinely mirrors the depth of knowledge creation or merely signals its absence. Through an analytical lens applied to both output production and underlying knowledge dynamics, this paper identifies an urgent necessity to recalibrate the current overemphasis on publication metrics in university assessments. By analyzing data on scientific output in direct comparison to the abstract concepts discussed, this research seeks a necessary shift in evaluation models. Ultimately, it advocates for a more balanced approach to measuring institutional success in universities. By prioritizing holistic measures over quantitative publication counts, educational evaluation systems can better reflect true institutional achievement. This refined perspective on evaluation standards in academia offers a more equitable framework for assessing university performance. Such a strategic realignment in how we evaluate institutions ensures a more comprehensive understanding of true educational achievement. This holistic evaluation approach ultimately supports more equitable assessments of institutional success across the university landscape.

This paper examines an OFDM system featuring an amplitude fading (AF) power line relay. In this model, information is sent over parallel carrier branches, where noise and interference from both the source and relay channels are aggregated into noise at the destination. The study derives the differential mutual information between the source and sink by integrating out the random phase of the fading channel across its Ricean distribution. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate the proposed framework.

Multi-channel waveguides serve a fundamental role in the development of integrated quantum technologies. The inclusion of atoms within these systems significantly boosts computational capabilities and enables novel dynamical behaviors. In this research, we investigate an atomic inclusion within a photonic channel where a specific segment is removed, resulting in an "atom-in-hetero-channel" system. This atomic setup interacts with two distinct arms characterized by different topological and channel nities. We demonstrate that by adjusting atomic parameters and inter-atomic distances relative to specific atomic settings, one can induce atomic Feshbach resonances. These conditions facilitate the generation of an atom-paratope state defined by specific resonance and scattering properties. Furthermore, our analysis reveals the feasible integration of an atomic T-mirror within such hetero-informed channels. Additionally, utilizing interference mechanisms between an atom-dimer configuration and an atom-monomer configuration, we propose constructing an atom-based multi-mode isolator operating within a single waveguide environment.

Foreseeing potential safety hazards at urban signalized intersections through a predictive approach offers a pathway to enhance driver and passenger experiences by lessening congestion-related annoyance, wear and tear, noise, and emissions. The anticipated advantages for automated vehicles (AVs) are even more pronounced. The current study introduces an informal predictive methodology for anticipating safety concerns as automated and non-navigable connected vehicles navigate a multi-lane junction, where non-navigable means vehicles that cannot alter driver behavior or receive real-time predictive data. Safety hazards specifically include collisions, excessive deceleration, discomfort levels, and decision-making opportunities for both AVs and their human-driven, uncontrolled counterparts. The proposed technique leverages decision-making strategies employed by AVs to forecast the trajectories of mixed traffic streams. By utilizing decision-based models, the system filters out the infinite possibilities of external environmental factors to identify a singular, most probable trajectory for each vehicle ahead. The control logic for the proposed scheme is twofold: first, the safety signal is generated by forecasting the movement of all entities; second, the control signal is determined by solving an optimal decision problem for the AVs. The solution to this optimal decision problem is derived using dynamic programming principles. The proposed control strategy is evaluated through extensive simulations. Imitation Learning (IL) excels at solving synthetic task environments by excelling where other methods struggle due to high sample inefficiency. A primary bottleneck preventing IL from reaching its full potential is the environment's overhead, which frequently slows execution to under 100 Hz. To address this, we introduce Text2IL, an implementation designed to run a broad spectrum of standard benchmark environments at approximately 10 MHz. Enabling solvent algorithms like PETS to cover six million transition during a single experiment, our approach yields state-of-the-art outcomes across seven standard environments—solving puzzles harder and faster than previous methods, cutting relative action error by 30% to 90% depending on the setting. To achieve such high performance, Text2IL employs multiple strategies, including the use of libmari, the elimination of GMP, and the removal of unnecessary overhead.

Short-term Long Term Networks (LSTMs) have emerged as the dominant deep learning architecture for video recognition, yet their massive floating-point operations and heavy parameter counts create significant computational and memory bottlenecks. To address this, we present a hierarchical Tucker-based local long-and short-term term network (HLTLTL), which hierarchically decomposes the weight matrices and kernels of standard LSTMs into local Tucker tensors. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate that this model not only retains strong recognition accuracy but also cuts computation and storage needs by roughly 99%. Furthermore, we designed an Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) system for hardware implementation that achieves a peak operating frequency of 500 Megahertz, utilizes 00 Megabytes of dynamic random-access memory, consumes just watts of energy per second, and reaches performance levels of operations per second.

In natural language processing (NLP), data augmentation serves to improve model performance by generating synthetic samples from existing datasets, addressing the challenge of high-quality annotation costs which often results in data scarcity. Although prior works have concentrated on scenarios where data scarcity involves low availability of labeled examples, the costs of automated self-labeling techniques are substantial, and current data augmentation strategies frequently neglect these synthetic labeling expenses. This study introduces a series of experiments across multiple models and language models to explore effective strategies for data augmentation that circumvent the overhead of pre-training or self-labeling, specifically designed for environments where enhanced data quality is needed to improve overall performance. Structural organizational patterns are pivotal in biological systems, ranging from molecular interactions to anatomical formations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these advanced capabilities stem from a deeper comprehension of tissue structure, as SONAN outperforms models trained on aggregated whole tissue section averages, which tend to obscure fine details. Finally, SONAN exhibits robustness in a unique setting: accurate cancer detection and grading across multiple pathology institutions using historically stored, varied whole tissue sections.

Current mobile robots typically map their environments using 2D occupancy grids, which serve as the standard for known settings. LiDAR technology serves as a critical sensor for remotely measuring distances and constructing 3D environmental models, capturing vast point clouds enriched with distance data and spatial coordinates. The origin of ultra-high-energy cosmic particles (UHECR) remains an unresolved challenge, as their sources must possess gravitational fields capable of accelerating particles to observed energy levels, defined by Oscar Loewenstein as the "source cutoff." Traditionally, these sources are identified as active galactic nuclei (AGN), characterized by supermassive central black holes accreating intergalactic matter. A significant proportion—potentially over half—of supermassive accreting black holes (SMBBHs) emit powerful neutrino outbursts during the ejection of relativistic jets, which accompany the primary accretion-driven jet. Consequently, UHECR sources could be a subset of all SMBBHs, specifically those emitting the powerful dual jets (one from accretion, one from the central black hole) necessary to accelerate UHECRs. If UHECRs originate solely from a minority subset of these sources, the resulting widespread high-energy neutrino emissions should create detectable sky clustering patterns. We propose testing this hypothesis by searching for spatial clustering among cosmological neutrinos, potentially observable by future detectors like P-TOLETO in Japan, which would confirm that UHECRs and neutrinos share a common source mechanism.

We analyze the link between multivariate functions and stationary processes, where functions are observed in time, space, or mixed time-space settings. Estimating these processes via singular spectrum decomposition involves first selecting appropriate dimensions and then determining singular vectors and eigenfields. Using dimension selection frameworks such as AIC and BIC, along with principal component analysis, we demonstrate that the interplay between multivariate functions and process theory enables more precise and high-dimensional estimation of process parameters. AES (Asset-Encumbered Stable Matching) frameworks, which have recently been adopted by prominent tech firms, have attracted considerable interest. These models are defined by the requirement that any card (or move) a student makes must be matched with a new one, ensuring that the total sum of pairings remains constant. Existing research has demonstrated that AES outcomes exhibit stable clustering and explainable tendencies toward matching majority preferences, defining these strong patterns as theoretical "stability" and a "predictive" nature. In this work, we show through both code and evidence that these models also display excessive sensitivity—termed "overstability" and "oversensitivity"—resulting in volatile pairings that diverge significantly from pure majority aims. We identify two primary drivers for these issues: first, the rigid constraint on the aggregate matching value; and second, the algorithm's tendency to assign new associates to applicants receiving numerous first-choice nominations but receiving few, if any, return matches themselves. To address "overstability," we introduce a method that relaxes the strict aggregate conservation rule. To mitigate "oversensitivity," we offer an improved algorithm that minimizes the disparity in new associate assignments by seeking a minimum-norm solution. Empirical tests confirm that implementing our proposed fixes leads to substantial enhancements in market-wide stability and reduced volatility.

This paper examines a one-dimensional random walk $X_n$ defined on a $2\delta$-narrow corridor with absorbing boundaries located at $\pm2\delta$. With steps having unit length and variance, we investigate the unnormalized correlation between walks that survive until time $k$ and those surviving until time $j$, specifically analyzing their behavior as $k$ approaches infinity. We introduce new findings concerning the connection between this random walk and the Gaussian free field. In addition, we establish an asymptotic formula for the probability that a walk survives, which is applicable beyond just unit random walks with integer steps and demonstrates convergence to the aforementioned free field. This result finds utility in estimating short-range correlations within isotropic random walks and calculating transition densities between Brownian motion processes constrained within narrow intervals.

Helicon plasma sources are recognized for achieving high electron temperatures and low plasma densities, making them ideal for diverse industrial applications such as material deposition, surface modification, waste treatment, and plasma-assisted combustion. In these systems, helicon mode transition occurs via electron cyclotron heating and wave mode conversion occurring in the magnetized regime. Controlling the transition from ordinary (O) to extraordinary (X) wave modes through axial magnetic field manipulation allows for effective thermal management of working surfaces, an attribute critical for industrial utility. However, diagnostic techniques suitable for this switch remain limited. This study employs passive and active diagnostic methods to analyze plasma characteristics during the O-to-X wave mode transition in the two-cavity helicon system of the IShTAR facility. Validation of the observed behavior was achieved by conducting comparative experiments with a standard single-cavity generator.

Microbial control agents are influenced by intraspecific competition, a factor this paper modelled within the context of pest management. Utilizing an existing biopesticide framework, we incorporated competition effects between beneficial insects and pest species. Our analysis reveals that introducing even trace amounts of competitors can drive the population of beneficial insects to collapse, a outcome that directly eliminates the stable equilibrium essential for effective pest suppression. Furthermore, the data indicates that as competition intensifies, the system may oscillate; notably, even minimal competitor counts can trigger Hopf bifurcations, leading to sustained cycles where pest numbers exceed equilibrium levels. We observed this dynamical behavior through numerical methods and validated it experimentally with colony-colony competitions of two *Coccinellidae* species, confirming that such interactions can indeed destabilize biopesticide populations.

Pyroptosis, a specific form of inflammatory cell death, has been observed in patients with severe SARS-CoV-2 infections, yet the precise mechanism by which the virus induces this outcome remains unclear. In this study, we established differential equations to model the interactions between SARS-CoV-2 infection and pyroptosis. Using experimental data to identify model parameters, we analyzed the dynamical systems to define the conditions for healthy homeostasis versus virus-induced pyroptotic cell death. Our findings indicate that virus-triggered pyroptosis arises when the infection shifts a healthy system dynamic toward cell death. Furthermore, we evaluated various anti-inflammatory strategies, identifying interventions that reduce viral load and mitigate inflammatory responses as most effective for preventing pyroptosis.

Reward function state variables often introduce unnecessary complexity, which can slow down reward learning and generalize learning. We propose an algorithm to identify and remove variables from the reward function learning variable states for Markov Decision Processes (MDCs). These variables are exogenous if removing them from the reward learning state does not impair the ability to learn an optimal policy. We provide a conceptual framework for these variables, introducing the concept of "endogenous" vs. "exogenous" variables. We introduce a novel algorithm to identify if an MDC has exogenous reward state variables and, if they exist, identify which variables they are. This algorithm is conceptually simple and efficient, running in near-linear time in the MDC dynamics' description length. We demonstrate through theoretical analysis and empirical evidence that these variables are frequently present in both learning and real-world applications, which supports the proposed framework. Our contributions include improved efficiency in both computational resources and data usage during reward learning, which results in clearer function definitions.

Decentralized applications built on blockchains often suffer lower performance and usability due to the need for on-chain verification of all computation, which can be alleviated by leveraging trusted off-chain preprocessors. This study introduces a new validator for smart contracts (Helmholtz) for Tezos based on refinement types that performs safe and efficient data transformations for associated smart agreements, with our approach offering key benefits: the capacity to validate transformed inputs derived from raw transaction hashes, source code generation in the language of choice, and the flexibility to incorporate user-defined behaviors. Comparisons with existing methods demonstrate that Helmholtz delivers superior efficiency, and we have implemented Helmholtz as an executable plugin for both Solidity and Tact development environments.

Deep learning has emerged as a prominent technique for denoising, largely due to its ability to generalize well. However, it often demands massive datasets for training, which creates prohibitive hurdles in Low-Dose Computed Tomography (CT) where acquired image counts are minimal. To address this scarcity, this paper introduces an enhanced Unsupervised Low-Dose CT Denoising method based on CycleGAN termed "AdaIN-Switchable CycleGAN." The core innovation lies in two key modifications: first, we incorporate Style Transfer via AdaBoost (AdaIN) into the CycleGAN architecture to strengthen generative capabilities and promote better unsupervised learning. Second, we implement a switching mechanism to integrate multiple generative networks, allowing the system to produce dose-reconstructed images tailored to various dose levels. As a result, this study presents a superior unsupervised framework capable of handling varying radiation doses. Experimental outcomes indicate that the proposed method surpasses existing state-of-the-art techniques, delivering superior denoising performance, higher structural fidelity, and linear intensity scaling across different levels of noise reduction.

Pre-training models using vast amounts of unlabeled data has yielded significant success in Common-Sense Knowledge and Factoid Question Answering tasks, such as CommonSenseQA and TriviaQA. However, dialogue comprehension benchmarks like MultiWOZ and CoChA-N often rely on pre-trained languages that struggle to effectively leverage both labeled and unlabeled training data available for these specific domains. To address this, we introduce SPACE-2, a tree-structured, self-supervised semi-supervised preprocessing framework tailored for dialogue understanding. Our framework includes two newly proposed loss functions designed to enhance entity and temporal expression recognition, as well as multiple newly created auxiliary tasks aimed at improving overall semantic representation. We conducted extensive experiments on the widely-used MultiWOZ and CoChA-N datasets, demonstrating that our approach achieves state-of-the-art benchmarks. Furthermore, our results indicate that only a minimal number of annotated examples are required to attain performance comparable to or exceeding that of large-scale semi-supervised setups.

This study explores the geometric configuration of an ideal fluid spacetime when endowed with a conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton according to the Sauty equation. As a consequence, these findings allow for the derivation of the exact metric expression for the (conformal) generalized Ricci-Yamabe soliton on the specified spacetime.

Precise predictions for the production rates of vector bosons in muon collisions are fundamental to achieving significant advancements in physics beyond the Standard Model. However, directly accessing the full differential distributions for two-body final states at next-to-leading order (NLO) presents substantial computational hurdles. Consequently, this study presents both conceptual frameworks and computational techniques grounded in the estimation of invariant phase space integrands, which have been enhanced by phase-function techniques and quasi-Monte Carlo algorithms. Leveraging established symmetry properties of NLO phase space elements around singularities, we derive normal distributions that accurately model the probability of phase space configurations. This statistical approach permits the separation of an NLO phase space element into quasi-integrand components, enabling the calculation of normal collinear and singularity factor corrections. Ultimately, normal distribution methods markedly enhance sampling efficiency, thereby yielding more rigorous predictions for vector boson physics.

This paper analyzes a model-based reinforcement learning approach where an actor and a separate, fixed director collaborate to collect training data. The director implements a consistent, task-agnostic strategy for exploring models and exploring environments across various settings. In contrast, utilizing a fixed exploration director module yields equal or superior outcomes, particularly when task-specific directors are employed. The provided numerical evidence supports these theoretical findings.

In Clifford algebra, the analytic functions that can be represented via a Cauchy integral formula using only monogenic kernels are defined as generalized analytic. Although many properties mirror those of complex analytic functions, no fundamental theorem capable of generating solutions from arbitrary data exists for the Clifford algebra's monogenic operator. By way of contrast, the current paper introduces a class of eigenfunctions tied to the Dirac operator through the Clifford algebra and demonstrates that this group adheres to a maximum modulus principle as well as a three-spheres theorem. Furthermore, it is established that the three spheres theorem serves as an essential basis for developing a theory of potential based on the mean value formulas.

Sequential estimation aims to produce unbiased bounds on a finite population's mean square error while maintaining geographically balanced mapping, a challenge often seen in surveying. Although many methods exist to achieve this balance, most are incompatible with statistical inference because they fail under the "no positive bias" criterion. This paper introduces a new geographically balanced sampling design that overcomes this limitation; it delivers balanced results with cut-square error rates comparable to existing optimal sequential estimation techniques.

This study examines the task of correcting camera intrinsic camera parameters using only one image, assuming access to corresponding eye-in-hand robot simulation data. A benchmark dataset for this purpose has been established, comprising 500 images captured by an ABB robot with a camera, where each image was obtained through a specific calibration process. A corresponding simulator environment has also been set up, allowing for the generation of 5000 simulated images matching the real-world scenarios. Experimental outcomes from both the simulated environment and the dataset derived from real images indicate successful learning, resulting in high-precision camera calibration from just one image.

Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks (CGANs) were originally developed to enhance supervised image segmentation, yet this study explores utilizing them to tackle T -type and/or ill-posed inverse problems. We establish a mapping between conditional generation and conditional inversion to derive a new operator, the regularized generative adversarial inverse (RGGI), governed by an $L_2$ regularization term and an associated dual, termed the regularized generative adversarial inverse dual (RGD). We demonstrate through a theoretical framework that the RGD functions as a data-fidelity consistency check on generated samples. Consequently, we propose two-dimensional conditional generative advection networks designed for generating both primary and checked aditional information (such as L2 norm images), enabling the extraction of solutions from the RGD framework. We highlight the flexibility of this method by showing how modifications to boundary conditions allow the model to incorporate various regularizers, thereby producing diversified and tailored solutions. Finally, we validate the proposed framework using two distinct test cases: a linear, one-dimensional (L2) problem and a nonlinear, multi-dimensional (MHD) problem with diversions, confirming the validity of the RGD approach and its associated models.

This paper proposes a reinforcement learning (RL) driven beam training protocol for multi-hop terrestrial communications. As a short-range technology, terahertz (THz) offers unprecedented unlicensed bandwidth, enabling massive data transmission rates. Nevertheless, significant path loss and severe phase fading due to molecular resonance require efficient hardware-based beamforming and precise beam alignment. The proposed RL-based framework jointly optimizes transmission and reception analog beams for every hop to maximize end-to-end spectral efficiency. By formulating the enhancement strategy as a Markov decision process (MDM), the study addresses the protocol's non-stationarity and high computational demands associated with exhaustive search methods. The approach builds on a structured exploration framework (SEF) to maximize learning efficacy, while introducing a spatially-structured experience replay method (SS-ESFR) that prioritizes sample utilization to accelerate convergence. Numerical results demonstrate that this RL method significantly surpasss traditional maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and random matching learning (RML) benchmarks in terms of optimal utility and convergence speed.

We conducted a comprehensive analysis of radio signal scintillation around the bright pulsar B1133+16, utilizing data from the Global Pulsar Observation Network (GPON) that spans 20 years. This analysis includes an examination of the intrinsic radio emission properties of the pulsar, a refinement of the signal model, and an investigation into the characteristics of interstellar turbulence. Our study highlights the necessity of accurately characterizing the intrinsic radio emission; the model improvement achieved this by refining the spectral index within the core emission region and by incorporating the radio absorption observed near 1.4 GHz. The latter is particularly significant, as previous research had overlooked this feature, which is now known to be substantial and variable on both timescales of hours and days. The absorption mechanism is likely tied to interactions between the pulsar's wind and ionized material in the Scorpius-Centaurus (Sco-Cen) association, specifically within its local bubble. Furthermore, our work offers a detailed description of two distinct turbulent cells located at wavelengths of approximately 1 pc and 10 pc. The larger 1 pc cell is dense and dense, likely comprising a mixture of Galactic cirrus and the nearby Perseus arm, whereas the 10 pc cell is sparse and cold, possibly associated with the local cavity of the Sco-Cen star-forming region.

This study introduces Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet), an innovative, pitch-aware, autoregressive neural network designed for speech synthesis. While the original WaveNet utilized dilated convolution to model the Markovian autoregressive process for probabilistic raw waveform generation, it lacked explicit pitch awareness and efficiency. To address these shortcomings, we developed QPNet, which integrates a novel pitch-sensitive dilated convolution built upon the principles of quasi-periodicity and the Short-Time Spectral Ampiltude (STSA) representation. In QPNet, the standard linear convolution applied within dilated units is replaced by specialized operations: the input audio is first transformed into STSA representations processed by a specific transformation, followed by application of QP filters. These adaptations enable the model to efficiently encode the sequential and temporal characteristics inherent in raw speech signals. Experiments indicate that the proposed QP filters are capable of learning the stochastic rules governing speech generation. Synthesis results demonstrate that QPNet outperforms the baseline WaveNet significantly, producing higher speech quality as well as improved diversity and accuracy in linguistic inference tasks.

Arabic relies heavily on morphologically driven agglutinative inflections, necessitating a robust preprocessing stage known as morphological analysis. This platform enables the correction of written and spoken texts, encompassing both regular morphological decomposition and irregular spelling changes. Built on a suite of advanced morphological algorithms, this platform delivers a user-friendly interface for researchers, linguists, and software companies working in the field of Arabic NLP.

Disentangling atmospheric compositions from the spectral signatures of photochemistry and atmospheric dynamics is essential for characterizing temperate, Earth-like exoplanets. We demonstrate the application of a novel machine learning framework designed to detect photochemical reactions within transmission spectroscopy data. By utilizing laboratory-measured spectra of small molecules (N$_2$, O$_2$, H$_2$O, CO, CH$_{4}$, and CO$_{2}$) as a baseline, we synthesized 10,000 synthetic transmission spectra for an atmosphere containing CH$_{4}$ and CO photochemistry. Our model achieved a 99.999% accuracy rate in identifying these reactive pathways. When used to differentiate a pure, non-reactive Earth-like twin (containing only CH$_{4}$ and CO without chemistry) from a synthetic planet with photochemistry, the system distinguished the scenarios 0.999 times out of 1000. These findings suggest that upcoming 30-meter class ground-based telescopes will have sufficient capability to confirm photochemistry in Earth analogs by analyzing their transmission spectra.

Detecting signatures of Majorana zero modes (MZMs) via spectroscopic tunneling methods is a suitable strategy for verifying them within topological superconducting platforms, such as those formed by semiconductor nanowires with proximitized s-wave pairing and transverse magnetic fields. A key challenge in this endeavor is differentiating the MZM signal, which peaks at zero bias, from spurious non-Majorana features that also appear at zero bias due to causes like impurities or stray modes. Consequently, distinguishing the MZM peak from these extraneous peaks is essential. In this work, we investigate Majorana tunneling spectra in a single-level quantum dot situated in a topological segment of a semiconductor nanowire, specifically examining how a resistance-loaded lead influences the system. We analyze this by comparing two scenarios: a fully conductive contact and a resistive contact. We find that while the presence of resistance yields the MZM peak distinctly, it may cause artifacts that mask or obscure spurious peaks entirely, without shifting them away from zero bias. Furthermore, we calculate optimal parameters for both the contact resistance and the electron-phonon relaxation time. Our results indicate that a high-resistive contact combined with slow electron-phonon relaxation facilitates clearer identification of the MZM peak, as it generates an asymmetric lineshape that helps differentiate it from symmetric, non-Majorana peaks.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) serve as a versatile framework for solving various problems involving graph data. Presently, we examine the generation of quantum states through field-assisted, energy-conserving, and scattering-mediated mechanical photon compression within an harmonic oscillator, utilizing both harmonic driving and a weak probe input. Analyzing the system via a quantum jump framework in the resolved sideband regime, we identify three distinct regimes in the low-loss limit, characterized by their respective non-linearities and coupling mechanisms. In the direct interaction scenario, optimal homodyne settings on the output field yield oriented cat-qubits; conversely, sequential application of phase rotations enables local optimization of mechanical displacement to produce stretching. Furthermore, when the system relies on intermediate thermal baths acting as intermediaries, we demonstrate the ability to create both optical and mechanical Fock superpositions by tuning the optical detuning relative to the compression parameter.

This extended abstract introduces a new variant of modal mu-calculus centered on directed trees distinguished by subnodes carrying "particles." We demonstrate that this directed tree structure constitutes an appropriate branching semantics for a heightened expressivity within the particle-enriched mu-calculus, specifically for properties pertaining to tree multiset ordering. Furthermore, we establish the computational hardness of both model checking and satisfiability for the scalar (single-state) fragment of this framework, finding that the latter problem reaches \(\Pi_1^1\)-completeness. Finally, it is shown that model checking for the complete multi-state system resides within PSPACE, while its satisfiability issue is contained in the arithmetic hierarchy's $A_2$ class ($A_2^{\rm arithm}$).

Exponential discounting, with its mathematical simplicity, has long dominated the modeling of intertemporal choice; however, its inability to capture the prevalence of preference reversals found in empirical data limits its efficacy. In this paper, we introduce an alternative, generalized exponential discounting function grounded in Tsallis entropy. Our framework effectively models preferences on both the consumption level and the time horizon dimensions and successfully accounts for preference reversals concerning consumption goods. Furthermore, assuming geometrically spaced temporal intervals, our analysis demonstrates how efficient intertemporal choice within this new model yields the foundational assumptions underpinning standard dynamic optimization techniques, including calculus of variations and discrete calculus methods such as Cramer's rule. We further establish that applying this discounting function within utility maximization scenarios produces path utilities adhering to a generalized logistic distribution. In the final sections, we offer a preliminary exploration of the implications arising from adopting this enhanced discounting structure.

Harmonic coordinate conditions, which function as partial fixed ones, are essential for the practical application of Substantial Gravity (also known as Substantive or Substantial Gravity theory). In our preceding work, we introduced a set of harmonic coordinates defined by specific physical requirements. The coordinates derived from these new requirements demonstrate superior behavior near the light-near singularity compared to harmonic conditions based merely on field equations. In this paper, we prove the uniqueness of these field-equations-based harmonic conditions and show that our physical conditions yield exactly. We also provide a direct verification method for these coordinates and establish their transformation rules under the associated coordinate transmutation.

In this study, we investigate limit groups and their connection to 2-torsion elements within the limited chromatic numbers of *signed graphs*—structures where edges are designated as either positive or negative. We demonstrate the existence of an extended version of the definitive 2-torsion double cover, which we term the **signed double cover**. Applying this construct, we establish a limit variant: the **limit 2-torsion double cover**. Our principal finding asserts that the family of all n-covers is sufficiently rich to distinguish limit groups; specifically, we prove that every limit group can be expressed as the homogeneous graph limit derived from such double covers.

The concept of negative absolute temperature ($T<0$), which has long existed within theoretical physics, recently sparked renewed curiosity on social media. Thisconceited renewal prompted a closer examination of the theoretical underpinnings behind $T \le 0$, considering both the classic Van Kranendonk and Purcell-Pound definitions. The paper argues that $T \le 0$ arises when a system's fundamental Hamiltonian exhibits a "sign-flip" symmetry, distinguishing it as a distinct physical entity separated by an infinite temperature interval ($|T|= \infty$) from all other standard thermal states. Furthermore, the study posits that because Hamiltonians supporting $|T|= \infty$ and $T<0$ differ structurally from those of conventional systems (where $0 < T < \infty$), strict thermal isolation is a prerequisite for these non-standard temperatures to exist. Finally, the authors assert that despite their atypical nature, systems at $T \le 0$ constitute genuine equilibrium states that can coexist in thermal equilibrium with conventional systems, provided the appropriate thermal equilibrium conditions are satisfied.

If $A$ and $B$ are finite, non-empty subsets of either the integers ($\mathbb{Z}$) or reals ($\mathbb{R}$), and $A^-$ denotes the subset formed by the absolute values of elements in $A$ (i.e., removing any signs), then there exists a constant $c$, dependent solely on whether the domain is $\mathbb{Z}$ or $\mathbb{R}$, such that $|A^- \pm (B)^+| \geqslant \frac{1}{C} |B|$ holds for all such subsets. In the specific instance of integers ($\mathbb{Z}$), the factor $C$ can be tightened to 2, whereas for reals ( $\mathbb{R}$), the factor $C$ can be improved to 3. Notably, this paper presents both lower and upper bound results, including precise conditions required to guarantee the inequality.

Colorectal cancer remains one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and is predominantly caused by the gradual transformation of healthy tissue within intestinal polyps (adenomas) into carcinoma. Microscopical analysis of these labeled biopsies enables clinicians to detect precancerous changes and plan subsequent procedures. Nevertheless, curated digital repositories of such datasets are frequently inaccessible, hindering the development of specialized machine learning models in this field. To address this scarcity, we present 'UniToPatho,' a comprehensive labeled collection containing 29,580 images of colorectal and other organs, analyzed across four levels of anomaly intensity from homogeneous to heterogeneous. We contributed open-label annotations to create a significant resource for research, thereby facilitating future work. To demonstrate their utility, we trained a convolutional neural network capable of distinguishing colorectal polyps and assessing adenomatous integrity with corresponding tags. Our findings reveal a robust model that differentiates healthy tissue from pathological formations and varies these lesions by intensity levels using only histological data. This technology offers a valuable aid for medical experts, enhancing efficiency and promoting greater collection availability through open-source availability.

We introduce a flexible finite element approach designed to address scattering problems featuring smooth coefficient gradients. To achieve smooth $H^{\infty}$ approximation of exponential functions, we employ Zernike polynomials within smooth mappings of standard finite elements. This method significantly broadens the High-Frequency Regime compared to conventional techniques, particularly when coefficients vary smoothly. The formalities regarding well-posedness and the applicable high-frequency regime are established, while a smooth dependence on high-frequency parameters is demonstrated within a high-frequency framework. Finally, the validity of the approach within a high-frequency context is demonstrated.

The formation of inner solar system planetesimals likely occurred through the aggregation of dust and ice, a hypothesis supported by two key lines of evidence. First, the Solar System's architecture implies that inner planetesimals accreted while surrounded by ice, as they currently possess low bulk densities that indicate an internal composition of roughly 50% ice. Second, numerous meteorites contain volatile elements and compounds, suggesting these planetesimals experienced interaction with liquid water at some point. Our findings reveal that Chelyabinsk and Benenitra, which are primarily composed of ice and silicate inclusions, exhibit distinct elemental signatures in their silicates resulting from exposure to water. Specifically, the Fe, Mn, Ni, and Cr within their silicates exist in oxidized states, and their Mg-Al-Mn profiles display unique characteristics. Laboratory heating experiments on various asteroidal silicate types demonstrate that such elemental patterns are characteristic of initial contact between water and ice-silicate mixtures. Furthermore, these patterns are effectively erased in later aqueous alteration processes. Consequently, the elemental data in these silicates provide compelling evidence that inner solar system planetesimals formed via the aggregation of dust and ice.

This work introduces the notion of relative quantum Topology for pairs consisting of a smooth surface and the divisor of curves with self-intersection zero, defined via an associated pro-surjective morphism to a surface of general type. We demonstrate that defining quantum topologies for surfaces possessing divisors is equivalent to defining them for surfaces of general type, and furthermore, show that the quantum topology categories preserve under specific surface modifications, including primitive surface flips and primitive primitive surface flips.

Although numerous deep learning models have been developed to diagnose pneumonia, there exists a lack of methods to adjust chest radiographs for improved model generalization. This paper introduces a novel, illness-driven image modification technique based on GANs specifically designed for radiographs. First, GAN-based noise addition and restoration algorithms were employed to train a classifier and extract pneumonia features from both healthy and affected radiographs, leveraging performance outcomes to isolate representative healthy RX samples. Subsequently, an illness-driven generator extracted components from both healthy and pneumonia radiographs to create a separation architecture comprising branches for healthy extraction, pneumonia extraction, and substitution. This setup enabled the isolation of both healthy attributes and pneumonia-specific atypical indicators fromX-RAY images, which were used to replace normal features inX-RAY images for constituting modified radiographs. Finally, these adjusted radiographs were utilized to train new classifiers, demonstrating an enhanced ability to diagnose both previously seen and unseen datasets.

Nonlinear visualization stands as a powerful and popular strategy for examining multi-dimensional vector datasets, which frequently contain inherent flaws such as noise, outliers, and voids. Effectively implementing this approach demands intuitive tools that enable data scientists to visually inspect datasets while adjusting visualization parameters to achieve the best results. Yet, existing options often fall short, either restricting access to clear visual representations of noise components or failing to offer user-friendly controls for its configuration. To address these deficiencies, we present ViDaExpert—an intuitive software application designed for the flexible visualization and review of multidimensional vector data. The program allows independent and linked modification of both data and visualization parameters. It empowers users to visually investigate various forms of noise by projecting data onto either two- or three-dimensional spaces through the visualization of expert-derived curves or surfaces known as ViDaMaps. By making the abstraction of noise visible and providing intuitive adjustment capabilities, ViDaExcel facilitates a more effective exploration of multidimensional datasets for optimal outcome generation.

This paper offers a precise evaluation of volume integrals representing Newtonian potentials evaluated on flat regions within $\mathbb{R}^d$ ($d \geq 2$). By deriving simplified expressions for these integrals, the work enables rapid computation of such terms in inverse problems, a capability demonstrated specifically within Electrical Resistance Tomography (ERT). This enhanced efficiency supports data-driven optimization of data assimilation strategies and improves the assimilation speed in problems involving forward problems.
